property_summary: After a successful schedule(target,value,data,predecessor,salt,delay), getTimestamp(hashOperation(...)) equals block.timestamp + delay, the operation is pending, and a second identical schedule reverts.
After a successful schedule with delay >= minDelay, the operation's timestamp equals block.timestamp + delay and the operation is pending.
After a proposer successfully cancels a pending operation, its timestamp becomes zero and the operation is neither pending nor a pending operation.
schedule always reverts when the caller does not hold the PROPOSER_ROLE, and leaves the operation timestamp zero.
Cancelling an operation that was never scheduled reverts and leaves its timestamp at zero.
An operation scheduled with a positive delay cannot be executed before its timestamp arrives: execute must revert with 'operation is not ready'.
A scheduled operation cannot be executed before its delay elapses; a failing execute leaves the operation pending and not done.
A pending scheduled operation can be cancelled by a proposer, after which its timestamp is zero and it is neither pending nor done nor ready.
Executing a scheduled operation marks it done: afterwards its timestamp equals 1 and isOperationDone returns true.
After an admin grants and then revokes PROPOSER_ROLE from an account, hasRole returns false for that account (and true between the two calls).
Granting the PROPOSER_ROLE to an arbitrary account makes hasRole return true, and its admin role is TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE.
Scheduling an operation with a sufficient delay sets its timestamp to block.timestamp + delay, so the operation becomes pending but not ready.
updateDelay reverts unless called by the timelock contract itself, and when it succeeds the minimum delay equals the new value.
An address without the PROPOSER_ROLE (the freshly deployed timelock's creator) can never successfully cancel an operation; cancel always reverts and the operation stays unscheduled.
The constructor grants TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE to the deployer, so an address holding it can grant an arbitrary role, and that role's admin is TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE.
grantRole on any role whose admin role is unset (bytes32(0)) always reverts and never grants membership, since no account holds the default admin role.
An account holding a role's admin role can grant that role to any account, and the grant takes effect (hasRole becomes true).
updateDelay always reverts when called by any address other than the timelock contract itself, and the minimum delay is unchanged.
After the timelock admin grants itself the proposer role, scheduling an operation with delay >= getMinDelay() succeeds and records its ready timestamp as block.timestamp + delay.
After an executor role is granted, executing an already-scheduled ready operation marks it done (getTimestamp == 1) and cannot be executed again.
For any operation, schedule reverts iff delay < getMinDelay() or the operation is already pending; otherwise it succeeds and sets the operation's timestamp to block.timestamp + delay.
